facts.text: I loved Bob the Builder as a child.
I was clumsily breaking serving bowls and vases as a child.
I broke my brother’s meticulous LEGO starships as a child.
My parents and brother unanimously agreed that I had a rare “reverse Midas touch.”
My family of engineers expected me to be naturally good at fixing things.
I was not naturally good at fixing things.
My favorite TV show taught me that building means more than mechanical precision.
I learned to love building communities by bringing people together.
I learned to use innovation and imagination to solve challenging problems in the world.
I became interested in working in edtech.
I witnessed the world fracture under social isolation.
I set out to build YAPA Kids.
YAPA Kids is an organization of high school volunteers.
YAPA Kids teaches and inspires young students.
I realized the power of technology to bring educational access and inspire younger students’ curiosity.
I am engaging with the Collins Institute.
I am working to develop personally tailored educational experiences enhanced by AI tools.
I have been interested in applications of AI in education.
I have a nature to tinker even if I break things.
I developed independent projects applying NLP topic and sentiment classification to email.
I developed independent projects using computer vision/CNNs to 3D MRI scans.
I resonate with the mission and vision of the Technology Innovation Fellows program.
This past summer, I worked as a Product and Engineering intern at Grata.
Grata is a growth-stage fintech startup.
At Grata, I pioneered the use of deep learning and NLP to make messy, complex financial information searchable.
I believe it is important to be involved in the policy and government perspective on technology.
I am currently taking a Gov seminar on disruptive technologies and international relations.
I spearheaded a white paper on large language models as a research project.
I applied for the Harvard Yun Fellows for Revolutionary Thinking program.
I conducted a year-long project into the effects of artificial intelligence on the workforce and economy.
I co-founded the Harvard AI Group.
The Harvard AI Group is affiliated with HCS.
I co-founded the Harvard AI Group to create conversation about AI on campus.
The Harvard AI Group allows for exchange of ideas.
The Harvard AI Group has 160+ members.
The Harvard AI Group holds events focusing on the impacts of AI on society, government, and technological advancements.
In a few weeks, we are planning to release free access to GPT-4 to the Harvard community.
I want to dive deeper into pursuing an entrepreneurial approach to the broader professional world, education, and policy.
Through the Undergraduate Technology Innovation Fellows program, I aim to leverage technologies including AI to create positive impact in the world.
I hope to learn and contribute my experiences as an engaged member of the ongoing conversation on technology at Harvard.
